props.name: font
props.description: The plain weight, `default` 500, `normal` 400 or `semi-bold` 600, the same in every theme. It replaces a level's themed weight. Not allowed with `typography`.

props.name: level
props.description: Document-outline level — `1`–`6` picks the rendered `h1`–`h6`. Defaults to `3`. The title keeps Heading's scale from before the theme roles in every theme: 24/33 at level 1, 18/24.75 at level 2 and 16/22 from level 3 down, all at 500, unless `size`, `font` or `typography` replaces it.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: size
props.description: A rung of the plain type scale, the same in every theme, at the snug 1.375 line height (`6xl` at 1.25). It replaces a level's themed size and line height. Not allowed with `typography`.

props.name: typography
props.description: A named heading style, `large`, `medium`, `small` or `xsmall`, which sets the size, line height and weight together from the theme at any level: `--heading-<style>-size`, `--heading-<style>-leading` and `--heading-<style>-weight`. External themes set the design's bold heading styles, 34/40, 28/34, 24/32 and 20/32 at 700, and internal themes 36/49.5, 30/41.25, 24/33 and 18/24.75 at 500. It excludes `size` and `font`; a JavaScript caller that passes them anyway gets the style. A `className` size, line height or weight still wins.

props.name: date
props.description: The event's date or instant. An HTML date or date-time string passes through unchanged onto the host `dateTime`, so a server and a browser in different time zones render the same value: a date (`2026-10-20`) or a date-time with an offset (`2026-10-20T10:00Z`, `2026-10-20T10:00+02:00`). A date-time without an offset names a different instant in each time zone, so development builds warn about one. A `Date`, or another string the JavaScript date parser reads (`June 15, 2024`, or `2024-02-30`, which it rolls over to March 1), is normalized with `toISOString()`. Every invalid value throws `RangeError("TimelineList.Time received an invalid date")`.
